lag_notes: Seconds_Behind_Master is 0 because the applier has caught up with what the receiver has, which is also true when the receiver is far behind the source.

notes: MySQL 5.7 records no queue or apply timestamps per transaction (they arrived in MySQL 8.0), so worker lag is not shown.

Seconds_Behind_Master compares the original timestamp of the event being applied with the replica's clock, adjusted by the clock difference measured when the receiver connected. A clock change on either server after that skews it, and one long transaction shows as a jump, so it is never the only lag signal.
